target_customer: Consumers in the UK and US buying telehealth care and online pharmacy products, including weight loss medication
problem: Consumer healthcare needs doctors and pharmacists at high cost per patient. AIOS aims to deliver care with very little human time per patient.
business_model: Direct to consumer telehealth and online pharmacy brands (Fella Health, Bolt Pharmacy) paid per prescription or order
product_category: AI enabled consumer telehealth and online pharmacy

founders.name: Richie Cartwright
founders.background_notes: YC page gives only the line about building a full stack AI doctor; no education or employers listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Telehealth and e-prescribing workflows are standard engineering; clinical safety and pharmacy compliance add hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Pharmacy and prescriber licensing is a barrier but many UK online pharmacies and telehealth brands operate; brands compete on price.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not sourced. Search found no dated evidence of what incumbents did to AIOS.

market_need_then: Telehealth and AI triage attracted funding in 2019 and 2020, and TechCrunch covered AI doctor apps such as Ada and Babylon. No AIOS specific demand evidence was found.

identity.visual_style: Operates consumer brands Fella Health and Bolt Pharmacy rather than selling under AIOS
identity.voice_and_tone: Company page uses bold unverified claims

brand_strength.rationale: Customers meet the Fella and Bolt brands, not AIOS; no press about the AIOS brand was found.

pivots.to: Owner of UK online pharmacy Bolt and branded telehealth supply
pivots.why: Sacra says AIOS acquired Bolt in April 2025; reasons not sourced.

outcome_analysis: AIOS appears active and says it is profitable, serving more than 150 thousand patients a month through Bolt Pharmacy after buying Bolt in April 2025, according to Sacra and the company's own pages. These claims, including a large revenue figure on the YC page, are unverified. Funding appears limited to small seed amounts, so growth looks capital efficient, but sources are thin and partly self reported.
notes: Seed amounts conflict across aggregators ($75K, $125K, $130K, $225K total) and none is verified; healthcarediscovery.ai reports no SEC Form D found; not recorded as rounds. Investors named by aggregators: Global Founders Capital, Streamlined Ventures, AngelList. The Notion page could not be read by the fetch tool. YC page says founded 2021 while Dealroom says 2020 and lists Gabe Campbell as co-founder; not added as a founder since no company or YC source opened says so. Sacra names Numan, Juniper and ZAVA as current UK rivals, not dated to 2020, so the competitor list is empty. Revenue claims such as $450M ARR are vendor stated and unverified.
